newsitem.title: CHINA: YUAN ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER VS DOLLAR IN SHANGHAI.
newsitem.headline: YUAN ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER VS DOLLAR IN SHANGHAI.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly higher against the dollar at 8.2893 on Thursday compared with Wednesday's 8.2896 on continued expectations of good trade figures for this month, dealers said.
After Tuesday's correction, the yuan regained its rising momentum, but buying seemed cautious, dealers said.
Trading was not active with most done at 8.2893, dealers said.
"The yuan maintained its stable movement at higher levels for nearly the whole day's trading," said one dealer.
"The market is interested in the the trade data that will be released in the next few days," he said.
"The surplus is expected to increase and will support a further rise in the local unit in the near-term," he added.
However, some investors were beginning to be more cautious about the yuan's future trend, another dealer said.
"With the expectation of good trade data already factored into the market, the yuan might fall slightly when the figures are released," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move above the 8.2900 level on Friday.
The yuan opened slightly higher at 8.2893 and showed stable movement in a narrow range of 8.2890 to 8.2895 for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2851 and a low of 8.2902.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2896.
The yuan closed slightly lower at 7.1481 from 7.1000 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intraday low of 1.0700 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
